newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tapie says gate money used in French soccer bribes.
newsitem.headline: Tapie says gate money used in French soccer bribes.

text.p: Failed tycoon and former soccer boss Bernard Tapie admitted to a French court on Tuesday that gate money from his Marseille team had been used to bribe rival players to lose a 1993 match.

"There was no need to use intermediaries to buy these matches, at least in the case of the money for Valenciennes -- it was cash from ticket sales for the European Cup final against Milan," Tapie said.

But pressed for details by a lawyer for the French Soccer Federation, Tapie, who is standing trial while serving out an earlier jail sentence for match-rigging and interfering with witnesses, quickly backed away from the statement.
"But I never said that," he responded when told what he had said. In any case, the disclosure was not a "scoop", he added.
"It certainly was a scoop. You have never said it before," responded the lawyer.

The 54-year-old rags-to-riches businessman, who also pursued a promising career as a politician before ending up in jail as bankrupt prisoner 265 449G, is accused of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million)from his Marseille club.

He went to jail three months ago when the French supreme court upheld his eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the Marseille case, which opened on May 12 and is expected to last another two weeks.
He faces a five-year sentence if convicted on charges of swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.

An investigating magistrate has accused Tapie of falsifying accounts to conceal bonuses and loans to players and illegally paying advertising companies based in tax havens to improve the image of soccer stars.
Tapie has said he can justify the sums that were spent.
His statement on the lack of need for intermediaries in the Valenciennes bribes came during questioning of Portuguese sports intermediary Miguel Barbosa by judge Guy Richarte.

Barbosa insisted a missing 2.3 million francs given him in connection with the transfer of Brazilian player Jose Carlos Mozer to Marseille from Lisbon's Benfica had not been used for bribes to throw matches.
Instead, he kept the money for himself, investing it in companies, Barbosa testified.
But Jean-Pierre Bernes, Tapie's former right-hand man, said he could not "rule out that this money was used to buy matches".
That prompted Tapie to interject that intermediaries were not required for such payments.
In later testimony, Tapie denied paying bribes for other matches to be thrown.
While Bernes testified that Marseille had bought victory in matches against Athens and Sofia, Tapie said the team "was approached twice during the Europe Cup finals, and we refused".
